Offer price divided by the undisturbed price, less 1, times 100.
Reported net debt including leases plus the two adjustments the expert makes.
The expert's other assets and liabilities between business operations value and enterprise value.
The middle of my adopted discount rate range, used to discount the table's cash flows.
Position in the table: 0 is the second half of FY25, 1 to 10 are FY26 to FY35. The count comes from the valuation and projection end dates.
FY25 revenue grown at my annual rate. The stub period is FY25 revenue less the first half already reported.
Revenue times an EBITDA margin that moves in straight lines from the FY25 margin to my FY30 margin and then to my FY35 margin. The stub period is FY25 EBITDA less the first half already reported.
EBITDA divided by revenue, times 100.
My annual corporate cost saving, scaled by the fraction of the year left in the stub period.
Revenue times a depreciation share that moves in a straight line from the FY25 share to my long-term share in FY30. The stub period is FY25 depreciation less the first half already reported.
Tax rate times (EBITDA plus the corporate saving less depreciation).
Revenue times my early-years rate to FY30 and my long-term rate after.
My working capital share times the increase in revenue over the prior year. The stub period takes the fraction of the year left.
Prior-year revenue times the share earned by the agents' businesses times the dividend rate paid to the agents. The stub period takes the fraction of the year left.
EBITDA plus the corporate saving, less tax, less capital expenditure, working capital and the agents' dividends.
Years from the valuation date to the middle of the period, or to its end if year-end discounting is chosen.
1 / (1 + base rate)^years.
